> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8c542a89bea8eb6ddab11b600a6f3f2f86111bd4` — the merge of head `0da73a49d58e7b7b2b7c3f5fb0c8a6f4db81b13d` into base `b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8c542a89bea8eb6ddab11b600a6f3f2f86111bd4 && git checkout 8c542a89bea8eb6ddab11b600a6f3f2f86111bd4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42 0da73a49d58e7b7b2b7c3f5fb0c8a6f4db81b13d && git checkout -B drift-repro b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42 && git merge --no-ff 0da73a49d58e7b7b2b7c3f5fb0c8a6f4db81b13d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `0da73a49d58e7b7b2b7c3f5fb0c8a6f4db81b13d`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #24827 (body; claim 6288623633; os-dev-report 6290825368). PR #24681's body (merged `12d14765c`), its FAIL record 6279650792 (B1: the Turso remote face's `{0, 0}` counts refused a fresh remote install) and its PASS record 6284464125 (the rule settled: the remote face counts created versus found from its own `sqlite_master` probe, `dceaa5646`; "cannot say" is still no). PR #24875's body (unchanged across the two heads), its file list (7 files, +412 / -5) and the net diff against merge-base `abd5acdaf` at the head `0da73a49d`, verified as the branch head on the remote; the delta `51849a38a..0da73a49d` read in full (one commit, one file, `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` +7 / -3, ①8); the head's check-runs (40 runs, 40 names, one read), and the prior head's for the red it carried. Cited code read at the head: `organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts` 195-262 and 330-600; `sql-driver.ts` 5626-5629, 12470-12560, 13496-13501, 13698-13718; `engine.ts` 12774-12789, 21535-21540; `schema-migrate.ts` 400-660, 810-819, 1280-1296, 1384, 1502-1504, 1594-1619; `apply.ts` 196-232, 296, 607-636, 711-721; `turso-driver.ts` 1059-1085, 4136-4158, 4209-4211; `remote-transport.ts` 1049-1050, 2097, 2101, 2269-2270, 2290-2297; `service-package/src/index.ts` 392-432; `scripts/check-optional-error-sink-contract.mjs` 1-250, 369-383, 496-518, 580-590 and its baseline; lint.yml 2926-2929.

### ① Derived judgments

**0. Gate verdicts on the head `0da73a49d`.** 27 `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, every Lint lane (ESLint; CI, release and engine gates; docs and code guards; repo and tooling gates; PM dispatch-gates; scoped: query-options erasure, slot lookup and corpus, tooling self-tests), every Type Check lane (workspace, consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger), Dogfood Regression Gate, the four claim guards, Auto Label, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, filter. **6 `in_progress`, NOT MEASURED: Test Core 1/6 to 6/6.** 7 `skipped`: the opt-in and main-only lanes (18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance). The prior head `51849a38a` was red on `Lint · docs and code guards` through `pnpm check:optional-error-sink` (lint.yml 2926-2929; its job 118625689260 step 63): the sink type ①8 removes. That red is this head's green.

**1. The one question — can a database that was NOT empty before `os migrate apply` gain the birth marker from it? No, on every case constructed.** The mechanism as read:
- The apply boots `deferSchemaDdl: true`, `deferredDdlUnsupported: 'skip-schema-sync'` (apply.ts 216-219). In `bootSchemaStack`, `skipSchemaSync` is true only for a Turso remote primary (`transportRefusesDeferredDdl` 810-819: driver `turso` and `detectMode` `remote`); `defer` is deferSchemaDdl and not skipSchemaSync (1286-1289). The deferral plugin exists on both postures (1384), `exemptPrimary` on skip-sync.
- On the deferred boot `SqlDriver.initObjects` stores each object in `deferredSchemaObjects` and `continue`s BEFORE the `hasTable` probe (12528-12531 against 12539-12547), so `tablesCreatedHere` and `tablesFoundExisting` stay empty and `getSchemaSyncStats` answers `{0, 0}` (13500-13501); the boot's birth plugin writes nothing. The two sets are instance fields written at 12546-12547 only, never cleared or reassigned anywhere in the file, so nothing ages or freshens them between boot and flush. No other `hasTable` call in the driver (7715, 11988, 13558, 14023, 14095) touches them.
- At the flush, `flushDeferredSchemaDdl` (13698-13718) takes EVERY deferred object — every object the boot synced, not the subset whose table is missing — clears `deferredDdl`, and re-enters `initObjects` with all of them; the re-entry probes each table (12539): absent → `tablesCreatedHere`, present and not created by this driver → `tablesFoundExisting`. After the flush the counts are this run's own observation of every declared non-rotation table on that driver (the dev measured `{created 1, existing 35}` on a populated file that gained one table).
- `recordBirthOfFlushedStore` (schema-migrate.ts 633-659) runs after every armed driver has flushed and after the package table's `ensure()` (1603-1611), and hands the engine to the runtime's own `recordOrganizationOwnershipBirth` (boot-guard.ts 419-434): `ledgerStoreCreatedFromEmpty` (477-485) reads the stats of the driver serving `sys_migration` (`ledgerStore` 462-469) and needs `existing` equal to 0 and `created` above 0; then `readMarker` must be `absent` (442-459); then `findV17ShapeTables` must be empty (238-262); only then `writeBirthMarker` (491-515). The engine fallback `wasDatastoreCreatedFromEmpty` (engine.ts 12774-12789) is reached only when the ledger's driver has no `getSchemaSyncStats` at all — a `{0, 0}` answer is an object, used as such, never a fallback.

The cases:
- **(a) Half-finished earlier apply, some declared tables present:** the flush re-probes all; the present ones land in `tablesFoundExisting`; `existing` above 0; no marker. Serve then refuses and names the ceremony. Fails closed; the body's "Interrupted runs" note matches. All present and no drift: the in-sync early return (apply.ts 296) precedes any flush; no call, no marker.
- **(b) Declared tables under different storage names:** the probe and the deferral key both use `StorageNameMapping.resolveTableName` (12522, 12529, 12539), the identity on the canonical name (a legacy `ns__name` prefix stripped; system-names.ts 287-290; Prime Directive #6, object name = table name). There is no second name to probe. A database holding tables only under names no object declares reads as empty on every declared table — and the serving boot's own `initObjects` would count the same and its guard write the same birth (551-570): equal to serve's verdict, not an admission serve would withhold. Every 17.x or 18.0 database holds the platform's `sys_*` tables under their declared names, the ledger `sys_migration` among them, so `existing` is above 0 there.
- **(c) Ledger table present but empty:** `sys_migration` is a declared object; `hasTable` true; found; `existing` above 0; no marker. Serve: absent marker, `existing` above 0, refused. Fails closed.
- **(d) Multi-driver stack, ledger on a non-default driver:** `ledgerStore` resolves the driver that serves `sys_migration` and reads that driver's counts alone. Every armed driver — the default, every `driver.*` service, every driver the engine holds or is handed through the `registerDriver` shadow (schema-migrate.ts 497-514, 541-560) — is flushed in the loop that precedes the birth call (1603-1605 before 1617). A telemetry sibling or a declared datasource neither ages a fresh primary nor freshens an old one: PR #24681's ruled rule ("judged on the driver of the store that holds sys_migration"), reproduced, not widened. A ledger on a non-SQL store: no stats, the fallback may read true, but `readMarker` is `inert` (no dialect, 446), not `absent`; return null, no write.
- **(e) Turso remote primary:** `skipSchemaSync` true, `defer` false; the primary is exempt from arming (`exemptPrimary` 480-485, 499, 522) so it is never flushed; the package table is planned only under `defer` (1503) so `ensure()` never runs there; the engine's boot sync is skipped so no remote schema door runs — `syncSchema` and `syncSchemasBatch` are the only two places the transport counts (remote-transport.ts 2097, 2101, 2269-2270) and the remote `applyMigrationEntries` calls neither. `TursoDriver.getSchemaSyncStats` on the remote face answers the transport's `{0, 0}` (4209-4211), an object, so no fallback; `created` above 0 fails; no marker. The first serving boot's remote face counts and births, the rule PR #24681's PASS record settled; unchanged here, and the body says exactly this. Not measured against a live `libsql://` store in this PR (the dev says so); the reading is from the code paths. Accept.
- **(f) Apply run twice:** over a marked database with nothing to do, the early return at 296 precedes the flush; with a table to create it flushes, re-probes all (`existing` above 0) and `readMarker` is `verified`; return null, row byte-equal. Pinned (c, d).
- **(g) An apply whose flush creates nothing:** reached only with drift and no pending creates; `flushDeferredSchemaDdl` still re-enters `initObjects` with every deferred object, so `existing` is the full count; no marker. With an EMPTY deferred set (a boot where the engine skipped its sync — `OS_SKIP_SCHEMA_SYNC=1` in the deploy environment, objectql/plugin.ts 431 — on SQLite, PG or MySQL), the flush returns `[]` and the only creation possible is `sys_packages` through `ensurePackageTable` → `engine.execute` raw DDL (service-package 423-428), which no counter sees; `{0, 0}`; no marker. Fails closed both ways.
- **(h) An engine where `getDriverForObject` is missing:** `recordBirthOfFlushedStore` returns before asking (644); the serving guard returns early on the same test (344), so no marker is owed. Consistent.

**2. The failed-write path.** `recordBirthOfFlushedStore` rethrows with `cause`, naming the row, the cause and the ceremony's two steps (648-657); `flushSchemaDdl` rejects (1617); apply.ts 636 sits inside the `try` at 235, whose catch (711-718) emits `{ error }` and `this.exit(1)` on `--json`, `printError` and `this.exit(1)` on the human face, with `finally` shutting the stack down. The command never reports success. Pinned by `schema-migrate.birth-after-flush.test.ts` (ablating the rethrow turned one case red, per the report). Not named in the text: the detected drift (`applyMigrationEntries`, 637) is left unapplied by the throw; a re-run re-detects and applies it, writing no marker since the tables now exist (③8).

**3. The guard's refusal rule and text, and the ceremony, are unchanged.** The runtime diff is the `OrganizationOwnershipBirthMarkerPlugin` docblock alone (366-374, +6 / -3; the hunk holds no code line). `organizationOwnershipRefusalMessage`, `assertOrganizationOwnershipMigrated`, `recordOrganizationOwnershipBirth`, `ledgerStoreCreatedFromEmpty` and `writeBirthMarker` are byte-unchanged. No `organization-ownership*` command or util is in the file list; `packages/drivers/**` and `packages/spec/**` are untouched. The hold-offs held.

**4. The fixture outside the claim** (`apply-organization-ownership-gate.integration.test.ts`, +4): a comment and one statement, `DELETE FROM sys_migration WHERE id = ?` with `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_MIGRATION_ID` (already imported there), after the `beforeAll` apply that builds `v18Db`. Only the marker this fix now writes, and necessary for both halves of that suite: cases 1, 1b and 1c read the marker's absence (`marker: null`), and case 3 inserts its own row under the same id, an INSERT the birth row would collide with. The same shape `organization-ownership-platform-global-column-drop.integration.test.ts` uses for its served boot.

**5. The pins.** `apply.organization-ownership-birth.integration.test.ts` runs the real command over a real file and reads the verdict through `assertOrganizationOwnershipMigrated` on a deferred read-only boot composed with the served platform, so `sys_migration` is registered and the guard is not inert — (b)'s refusal is the control (118-134). (b) drops `sys_platform_setting_audit` so the flush creates exactly one table in a populated unmarked database, asserts `created` is that one `create_table` (the trap the body names) and `markerRows` empty; its 17.x arm adds a physical `organization_id` on `sys_platform_setting` and asserts the refusal names that table. Red on main for (a) and (c, d) per the report; ablating the emptiness check turned (b) 18.0 red with a false birth row — the ablation that proves the decision is the counts, not the returned work. New files are in the tsconfig program (2 of 2, per the report).

**6. Public surface.** `recordBirthOfFlushedStore` (new export) and `DeferSchemaDdlPlugin.logger` (new public field) live in `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts`, which `@objectstack/cli`'s `exports` (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`) do not reach and `src/index.ts` does not re-export: CLI-internal, as declared. What `@objectstack/cli` publishes differently: `os migrate apply` writes one `sys_migration` row on a database it created from empty, and exits 1 when that write fails. `@objectstack/runtime` publishes nothing different; `recordOrganizationOwnershipBirth` was already its export (PR #24681). No spec, no schema, no governed path, no fork (head repo is the base repo).

**7. A wording gap, no behaviour:** the `if (deferral)` at 1617 and its comment "only a deferred boot" — the skip-sync boot's deferral is non-null too (1384), so the Turso remote apply enters the birth half and leaves on `{0, 0}` (①1e). Harmless; ③9.

**8. The delta `51849a38a..0da73a49d` is type-only, with no behaviour change.** One commit, `schema-migrate.ts` 588-600: the alias `type BirthLogger = { info?: ...; error?: ... }` (an optional `error` beside no `warn`, the `no-fallback` shape `check-optional-error-sink-contract.mjs` reds at 509-515, unbaselined) is replaced by `type BirthLogger` equal to `Parameters` of `RecordOrganizationOwnershipBirth` at index 1 — the runtime's own parameter, `{ info?: ... }` or undefined (boot-guard.ts 421) — with a docblock saying why: nothing on this path logs a failure, it is thrown (①2). Its two uses are unchanged in text and widen nothing: the field `logger: BirthLogger | undefined` (477, assigned `ctx.logger` at 498) and the parameter at 636, handed straight to `recordBirth(engine, logger)` (646), whose own parameter type it now is. No expression, statement, call or export moved; the three test files, apply.ts and the runtime are untouched by the delta. Under the gate's population rule (an interface, a type alias to a type LITERAL, or an inline type literal, 582-586) an indexed-access alias is none of the three, and the only literal left on the path — the runtime's parameter — declares no `error`, so it was never in the population. Measured: every Lint and Type Check lane `success` on this head (①0). The PR body still reports its runs on `51849a38a`, which a type-only delta does not invalidate.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli: minor` with `Clause-②: yes`, no arm, on the changeset and the PR body alike. The level axis of `check-changeset-no-major` (its header, items 1 and 2): a PR declaring clause ② must grade at least one package whose published source it moves `minor` or above — the cli is that package — and no `major` is introduced (the launch-window guard; Check Changeset `success` on this head). `yes` fits the content: the boot guard's admission set gains one writer (a database `os migrate apply` created from empty is now served); nothing an author writes moves, no export is removed, so no arm and no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `minor` is the floor `yes` takes (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3) and is what the diff publishes: a behaviour a published command did not have. The runtime's docblock-only change takes no changeset, rightly; the delta changes no published surface and owes none. Tier: the committed tree carries no published schema, no governed path and no `(narrowing)` line, so this is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT` by the template's rule, whatever depth the claim said the seat would read at; the reading above is the cited code in full.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's deviations (report 6290825368), each answered:
1. A one-object scratch project, not `examples/app-showcase` (74 tables against 71): the mechanism is the deferral and the flush, not the object set, and the refusal text is the same. Accepted.
2. Red-on-main and the runtime ablation ran on `495889a0e`, before the main merge: between that head's base `41646a578` and the final base `abd5acdaf`, main's 7 commits touched none of `schema-migrate.ts`, `apply.ts`, `organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`, `sql-driver.ts`, `engine.ts` or `standalone-stack.ts` (`git log` over those paths is empty), so both legs transfer; the later delta (①8) changes no code those legs ran. Accepted.
3. The CLI integration tier filtered to migrate and organization-ownership; the full runtime suite not run: declared narrowings; CI's Test Core 1 to 6 are the measure and are NOT MEASURED at this read (in progress on `0da73a49d`). The seat reads them before queueing. Carried.
4. One locked run exit 99 (queue timeout) re-run; one foreground wait resumed with `tail --pid`: process hygiene, nothing redone. Accepted.
5. Trailers: the model-free pair on the four authored commits (the delta's included) and the harness's model-named form not used — that is AGENTS.md's rule. The merge commit `0be22e895` carries no trailer pair, a gap against "an agent commit ends with the pair"; no hook refuses it and the PR body carries the session URL. Noted, not blocking.
6. Not re-merged after opening (12 commits behind at this read; GitHub reports `blocked`, not `dirty`): Multi-agent discipline §10 merges only on a conflict, a main-caused red or a queue removal. Since the base, main's `df8bb40a0` (#24845) touched `sql-driver.ts` only at 94, 5703, 7773, 8136, 8397, 8431 and 12130 — not the counting seam (5626-5629, 12539-12547, 13500, 13698) — so ①1 holds on the queue's rebuilt tree. Accepted.
7. `recordBirthOfFlushedStore` exported for the unit pin: CLI-internal (①6). Accepted.

Not in the report: the patch round itself (①8) carries no os-dev-report on the card and no PR comment at this read; its commit message states the reason, and the dispatch-gates note at the gate's line 232 (REFUSE-WIDE: no path derives `check:optional-error-sink`) explains why the dev's 68-gate sweep could not see the red on `51849a38a`. Named here so the record of the round is on the card; not blocking.

Other flags, none blocking:

9. The "only a deferred boot" comment at 1617 (①7). Wording; carried.

11. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` is not edited; its sentence "the first boot that creates a datastore from empty writes a birth marker" now covers `os migrate apply`. The Docs Drift Check names 9 hand-written pages and 4 release-owned (read-only) ones. A sentence naming the apply would be a nicety. Carried.
12. The Turso remote path rests on `transportRefusesDeferredDdl` → `exemptPrimary` → never flushed, read in code, with no live `libsql://` measurement in this PR; PR #24681's kernel pin covers the serving birth there. Carried.
13. #24833 (`os dev`'s recover text) follows this card, per the claim.
